name: Shillong
description: Capital city and district headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Scenic hill station at about 1,496 m elevation with colonial charm, pine forests, lakes, waterfalls, and as the cultural and educational hub of the Northeast.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills and capital of Meghalaya
Average elevation around 1496 metres
About 100 km from Guwahati airport/rail
Known for educational institutions and music scene

name: Khliehriat
description: Headquarters of East Jaintia Hills district, a plateau town serving as the administrative and commercial centre for the eastern Jaintia region. Gateway to remote caves, waterfalls, and border areas near Bangladesh.
facts: HQ of East Jaintia Hills since district creation in 2012
About 55-60 km east of Shillong
Elevation around 700-750 metres
Base for exploring Shnongrim caves and southern waterfalls

name: Krem Liat Prah
description: Longest natural cave system in India and South Asia, with surveyed passages exceeding 34 km on the Shnongrim Ridge. Features vast chambers including the Aircraft Hangar, underground streams, and ongoing exploration by international caving teams.
facts: Current explored length about 34 km and still growing
Located near Shnongrim and Larnai villages
Requires guided expedition; not for casual visitors
Part of larger cave network with ~150 caves on the ridge

name: Nongkhnum River Island
description: Largest river island in Meghalaya (about 21-25 sq km), formed by the bifurcation of the Kynshi River into Phanliang and Namliang branches. Features sandy beaches, grassy meadows, suspension bridge, and nearby waterfalls; low tourist footfall due to remote access.
facts: About 14 km from Nongstoin, West Khasi Hills HQ
Second-largest river island claims often overstated for tourism
Activities include boating, fishing, picnics on meadows
Includes Weinia and Langshiang Falls nearby

name: Langshiang Falls
description: Tall plunge waterfall on the Kynshi River near Sangriang village, about 24 km from Nongstoin. Quoted height around 337 m (1,106 ft), one of the highest in the region, with dramatic cliffs and panoramic valley views; also called Kshaid Ur-Nar.
facts: Height generally quoted at 337 metres, among India's higher falls
About 24 km / 15 mi from Nongstoin; 30-min walk from Sangriang
Visible from Mawpon village; part of Kynshi system
Best after monsoon for full flow; remote access

name: Weinia Falls (Kshaid Weinia)
description: Scenic waterfall on the Kynshi River near Nongkhnum River Island, about 14-15 km from Nongstoin. Features powerful cascades into a gorge with a wooden bridge, rocky cliffs, and nearby picnic spots; lesser-known but dramatic.
facts: Near Nongkhnum Island and Langshiang Falls
Height around 60 m in some descriptions; part of river system
Accessible via Nongkhnum Road; short walk to viewpoint
Low crowds; combine with island visit

name: Nongstoin
description: Headquarters town of West Khasi Hills district, at about 1,409 m elevation. Serves as the main gateway to Nongkhnum Island, Langshiang and Weinia Falls, and other western Khasi attractions; administrative and market centre.
facts: District HQ of (current) West Khasi Hills; population ~28,742 (2011)
About 90-100 km west of Shillong via NH
Elevation ~1,409 m; cool climate
Base for exploring river island and falls

name: Mairang
description: Headquarters town of Eastern West Khasi Hills district, at about 1,564 m elevation. Gateway to Kyllang Rock, Mawthadraishan Peak, Markham Valley, and other central Khasi attractions; administrative and cultural centre with colonial-era elements.
facts: HQ of Eastern West Khasi Hills (carved 2021 from West Khasi Hills)
About 40 km west of Shillong on NH 106
Elevation around 1,564 m
Base for exploring Kyllang Rock and nearby peaks

name: Mawthadraishan Peak
description: Highest peak in Eastern West Khasi Hills at 1,924.5 m (6,314 ft), midway between Mairang and Nongstoin. Offers panoramic views of Assam plains, Garo Hills, Khasi ranges, and distant Himalayas on clear days; features small fish ponds at the summit.
facts: Highest elevation in the district at 1,924.5 metres
Located near Mawroh, Markasa and Nongshillong villages
Accessible via short trek from Shillong-Nongstoin road
Panoramic views including parts of Bangladesh on clear days

name: Kyllang Rock
description: Massive granite monolith dome rising from pine forests near Mairang, about 1,774 m elevation and ~300 m wide. Steeped in Khasi folklore (personified as a man in legends involving Thadlaskein and Symper Rock); short climb offers panoramic views of valleys and villages.
facts: About 9-12 km northwest of Mairang
Elevation around 1,774-1,800 m; dome ~300 m across
Accessible from northern/eastern flanks; southern steep
Rare white rhododendrons at base; best Oct-Apr

name: Markham and Remkhla Valley
description: Rolling highland meadows and valleys near Markham and Mawkyllei villages, locally known as Laitmurok viewpoint. Known for misty mornings, green hills, grazing lands, and as a lesser-crowded 'Mini Dzukou' experience between Eastern West and South West Khasi Hills.
facts: Situated in Markham and Mawkyllei villages
Popular for scenic views, photography, and slow travel
Misty mornings and lush post-monsoon landscapes
Accessible via intermediate roads from NH 44E/106

name: Ka Phan Nonglait Falls
description: Serene waterfall in Eastern West Khasi Hills, surrounded by lush forests. Named after an unsung warrior who fought the British; offers a peaceful atmosphere for nature lovers and photography.
facts: Named after unsung warrior against the British
Surrounded by dense green forests
Official district tourism attraction
Accessible via intermediate roads from main highway

name: Tirot Sing Ecological Park
description: Park at Mairangbah village featuring a colonial-era pine tree, statue of U Tirot Sing (Khasi freedom fighter in Anglo-Khasi War 1829-1833), children's play area, and views of sunrise/sunset over Mairang Town.
facts: Features statue of U Tirot Sing and colonial pine tree
Located at Mairangbah village
Good views of Mairang Town
Combines history, nature, and family recreation

name: Mawkyrwat
description: Headquarters town of South West Khasi Hills district, formed in 2012 from West Khasi Hills. Serves as the main administrative and market centre and gateway to hot springs, caves, plateaus and border areas of the district.
facts: District HQ of South West Khasi Hills since 2012
Elevation around 1,360-1,500 m
About 70-80 km southwest of Shillong
Base for exploring Jakrem, Ranikor and Iawpaw

name: Jakrem Hot Spring
description: Natural sulphur hot spring on the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road at Lawblei (Jakrem), about 15 km from Mawkyrwat and 60 km from Shillong. Believed to have medicinal properties; popular for bathing and picnics in winter with bathing compartments available.
facts: Sulphur-rich thermal waters with claimed curative properties
About 15 km from Mawkyrwat, 60 km from Shillong
Favourite winter picnic and bathing spot
Official district places-of-interest

name: Symper Rock
description: Unique geological rock formation about 50 km from Shillong on the western side of the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road. Offers views of the Mawkyrwat area from its top; associated with Khasi folklore involving legendary battles with Kyllang Rock.
facts: Unique geological formation on Shillong-Mawkyrwat road
Views of Mawkyrwat area from the top
Linked in folklore to Kyllang Rock
About 50 km from Shillong

name: Umngi River
description: Longest river in Mawkyrwat subdivision, about 18 km from the town. Favourite picnic spot with a small river island where beach volleyball is played; source starts from Sohiong and stretches toward Umpung lake.
facts: Longest river in Mawkyrwat sub-division
About 18 km from Mawkyrwat
Small river island used for beach volleyball
Source from Sohiong area

name: Phlangja Ud Cave
description: Beautiful cave about 16 km from Mawkyrwat at Phlangja Ud, south of Rangmaw village. Features hanging stalactites; above the cave is a vast grassland offering views of the Bangladesh plains. Cave length about 600 meters.
facts: About 16 km from Mawkyrwat near Rangmaw
Stalactites on the ceiling
Grassland above with views of Bangladesh plains
Cave distance around 600 meters

name: Rilang View Point
description: Beautiful valley and viewpoint about 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang on the Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road. Meandering across the river, it is a convenient picnic and angling spot.
facts: About 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang
On Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road
Picnic and angling spot
Views of meandering river valley

name: Synrangbah Cave
description: Yawning open cave at Nonglang, about 3 km from Mawkyrwat. The Mawkyrwat-Photjaud road passes through the leveled inner part; used as shelter by people and cattle during rain, home to bats of various sizes.
facts: About 3 km from Mawkyrwat at Nonglang
Road passes through the cave
Shelter during storms for people and cattle
Inhabited by bats

name: Dongnob Falls
description: Beautiful waterfall about 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud. Features a cave in the middle of the falls that becomes a splendid natural beauty in winter with the reflection of sun rays.
facts: About 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud
Cave in the middle of the falls
Especially beautiful in winter with sun reflections
Official district tourism spot

name: Iawpaw Plateau (Nongnah)
description: Beautiful plateau village about 30 km from Mawkyrwat, southwest of Nongnah. Offers bird’s-eye views of surrounding hills, valleys, Bangladesh plains and rivers, and distant Himalayas. Features a long cave; looks like a bed from a distance according to legend.
facts: About 30 km from Mawkyrwat near Nongnah
Views of Bangladesh plains, rivers and Himalayas
Longest cave in Khasi Hills located on the plateau
Tableland appearance from a distance

name: Ranikor
description: Border town about 45 km from Mawkyrwat on the bank of the river near Bangladesh. Formerly a winter resort of the queen of Maharam; known for angling Golden Mahseer, boat rowing, and the Borba Singh Bridge (second-longest suspension bridge in India). Hosts an annual tourism festival.
facts: About 45 km from Mawkyrwat, near Bangladesh border
Best spot for Golden Mahseer angling
Borba Singh Bridge over the river
Annual tourism festival in February

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India, dropping about 340 metres (1,115 ft) from the southern edge of the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Dramatic cliffs, mist, and views toward the Bangladesh plains; associated with the Khasi legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Height ~340 m / 1,115 ft; tallest plunge in India
About 5-7 km from Sohra (Cherrapunji)
Fed by highland rainwater; strongest in monsoon
Official East Khasi Hills tourism highlight

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall about 12 km from Shillong city centre in Upper Shillong. Mountain stream descends through successive falls amid fern-covered rocks; easy access via paved paths and bridges. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong on outskirts
Three successive falls (main and two smaller)
Paved footpaths and wooden bridges
Popular short outing from the city

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m (6,446-6,449 ft), roughly 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, waterfalls, and distant Bangladesh plains on clear days. Access requires photo ID at the Air Force viewpoint.
facts: Highest elevation in Meghalaya ~1,965 m
About 10 km south of Shillong city
Panoramic views including Bangladesh plains
ID required; cameras may need to be surrendered

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in Pynursla block near the India-Bangladesh border, widely recognized as one of Asia’s cleanest villages. Features living root bridges, balanced rock, bamboo dustbins, high literacy, and community-managed eco-tourism with homestays.
facts: Awarded cleanest village in Asia (Discover India 2003)
About 90 km from Shillong near Bangladesh border
Living root bridge and balancing rock attractions
100% literacy reported; Khasi matrilineal society

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus roots by the Khasi community in Nongriat village. Reached by a steep descent of roughly 3,000-3,500 stone steps from Tyrna; unique bio-engineering example with natural pools and optional Rainbow Falls extension.
facts: Located in Nongriat village, ~15 km from Sohra
Trek from Tyrna involves ~3,500 steps
Two stacked tiers for high-water safety
Community-maintained living structure

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong near Smit. Deep gorges, ridgelines, cloud-shadowed valleys, and panoramic highland landscapes; popular for photography and half-day outings.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong; nearest major village Smit
Dramatic ridgelines and deep gorges
No direct buses; taxi or tour recommended
Best in clear post-monsoon weather

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) protected for centuries by Khasi traditional beliefs about 25 km from Shillong. Dense old-growth forest with high biodiversity; nothing may be removed, not even a leaf. Guided walks available.
facts: About 25 km southwest of Shillong
Protected by Khasi customary laws for centuries
Rich in orchids, ferns, and endemic species
Strict rule: take nothing out of the forest

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra (Cherrapunji), about 150 m of illuminated passages with stalactites and stalagmites. Safe for beginners and families; short forest approach.
facts: About 6 km from Sohra town
Lit route ~150 m; suitable for beginners
Stalactite and stalagmite formations
Paired with nearby Nohsngithiang Falls

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Segmented waterfall dropping about 315 m over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai village, forming seven parallel streams in monsoon. Overlooks the Bangladesh plains; also called Seven Sisters Falls.
facts: Height ~315 m; segmented into seven parts
About 1 km south of Mawsmai village
Best in monsoon for full flow
Views toward Bangladesh plains

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Sub-divisional town on the southern Khasi plateau, historically one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to Nohkalikai, Mawsmai, Nohsngithiang, living root bridges, and views over the Bangladesh plains. Elevation about 1,430 m.
facts: Local and official name Sohra; formerly Cherrapunji
Average elevation ~1,430 m
About 54-60 km from Shillong
Base for major East Khasi waterfalls and caves

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong, planned in the 1890s. Surrounded by botanical gardens, cobblestone paths, a wooden bridge, boating, and flower beds; also known as Pollock Lake or Nan Polok.
facts: Built 1894; designed by Fitzwilliam Thomas Pollok
Central location near Raj Bhavan
Boating facility and botanical garden
Popular short visit in the city

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Seven-storey hexagonal museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artefacts, costumes, and traditions of Northeast India’s indigenous communities. Major cultural attraction with galleries, research facilities, and city views.
facts: Seven floors representing Northeast states
Located in Mawlai Phudmuri, Shillong
Ethnographic collections of tribal cultures
Popular with students and cultural visitors
